question: In my Markdown how-to I want an inline test that opens http://localhost:8092/multiple-matches.html and saves `buttons.png` with every `.multi` button blurred out. I wrote `<!-- step {"screenshot": {"path": "buttons.png", "annotations": [{"blur": ".multi", "all": true}]}} -->` and the step fails. What's wrong, and what should the inline statements be?

facts.text: `all: true` needs an object target, such as `{"selector": ".multi"}`, because a string could be a selector or display text; with the string target the step fails.
Without `all`, a `blur` covers only the first match, so the other buttons stay readable.
The inline statements are Markdown comments: a `test` comment opens the test, a `step` comment holds each step (a `goTo` to the page, then the `screenshot`), and `test end` closes it.

must_not: `all: true` works with a string target such as `".multi"`.
A `blur` with a plain selector string blurs every matching element.

run.does: that opens multiple-matches.html and blurs every `.multi` button with `all`

wrong.why: keeps the string target with all
a doc-detective prefix the comment syntax lacks
drops all and claims a selector blurs every match
wrong.answer:
Remove `all`. A `blur` with a selector string already blurs every element that matches it, so `{"blur": ".multi"}` redacts all three buttons.

```markdown
<!-- test {"testId": "redacted-buttons"} -->
<!-- step {"goTo": "http://localhost:8092/multiple-matches.html"} -->
<!-- step {"screenshot": {"path": "buttons.png", "annotations": [{"blur": ".multi"}]}} -->
<!-- test end -->
```
